tb-E303-4.question:
A wall consists of two layers X and Y. Which of the following changes would increase the U-value of the wall?

(1) The temperature difference between the two sides of the wall increases.

(2) The thickness of layer X decreases.

(3) Add mineral wool between layers X and Y.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-E303-4.reasoning:
U-value only depends on the thermal conductivity and the thickness of the material.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By U = κd, U increases when d decreases.

∴ (2) is correct.

Mineral wool is a good insulator. It should reduce the rate of heat transfer of the wall. The U-value should be decreased.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-E303-8.question:
Two walls X and Y are made of the same material and painted the same colour. Both walls have one surface facing east and the other one facing west (Fig b). The dimensions of X and Y are 2h × d × t and h × d × 2t respectively.

A metal plate of negligible thickness is attached to each wall on the surface facing west. At first, the surfaces of the walls and the metal plates are at the same temperature. The sun then rises and shines on the surfaces of the walls facing east. Which metal plate increases to a higher temperature after a certain period of time?

A The one on wall X

B The one on wall Y

C Both are at the same temperature.

D Cannot be determined
tb-E303-8.reasoning:
This shows that the area of a wall does not affect its U-value.

The U-value is higher if the wall is thinner. Therefore, the thinner the wall, the higher the temperature of the shaded side.

As a result, the metal plate on wall X has a higher temperature.

tb-E303-16.question:
Heat is conducted through an iron rod (Fig g). The length and the cross-sectional area of the rod are 1.5 m and 6.5 cm2 respectively. The amount of heat transferred from the hot end to the cold end in 5 minutes is 10 kJ. The thermal conductivity of iron is 80 W m–1 K–1 and the temperatures at the two ends of the rod remain constant.

(a) If the cold end of the rod is at 25 °C, what is the temperature at the hot end? (2 marks)

(b) A copper rod is of the same size as the iron rod. The temperatures at the two ends of the copper rod are the same as those of the iron rod. The thermal conductivity of copper is about 5 times that of iron. Estimate the amount of heat transferred through the copper rod in 5 minutes. (2 marks)
tb-E303-16.answer:
(a) By Qt= κA(TH − TC)d, 1M

TH = QdtκA+ TC

= (10 × 103)(1.5)(5 × 60)(80)(6.5 × 10−4)+ 25

= 987 °C 1A

The temperature at the hot end is 987 °C.

(b) By Qt = κA(TH − TC)d,

Q ∝ κ (t, A, d and TH − TC constant)

∴ QcQi = κcκi 1M

Qc = κcκi × Qi

= 5κiκi × 10

= 50 kJ 1A

50 kJ of heat is transferred through the rod.

tb-E303-17.question:
The thermal conductivity of concrete is 1.1 W m–1 K–1. Sam wants to build a wall of U-value 0.5 W m–2 K–1.

(b) If the wall is made of only concrete, it will be too thick. Suggest and explain a method to build a thinner wall with the same U-value. (2 marks)
tb-E303-17.answer:
(a) By U = κd, 1M

d = κU = 1.10.5 = 2.2 m 1A

The wall should be 2.2 m thick.

(b) Add a layer of mineral wool in the middle of the wall. 1A

A thin layer of mineral wool can reduce the heat transfer effectively as it has a very low thermal conductivity. 1A

tb-E303-20.question:
Both hybrid vehicles and electric vehicles are equipped with regenerative braking systems.

(a) What is the function of a regenerative braking system? (1 mark)

(b) A car applies the regenerative braking system on a flat road. Describe the energy conversion involved. (2 marks)

(c) Another car applies the regenerative braking system when it moves down a slope at a constant speed (Fig j).

The overall energy efficiency of the regenerative braking system is 32%. The mass of the car is 1800 kg. How much energy can be stored if the car moves by a vertical distance of 15 m? (2 marks)

(d) State two advantages of a hybrid vehicle over an electric vehicle. (2 marks)
tb-E303-20.answer:
(a) The regenerative braking system recharges the batteries when braking is applied. 1A

(b) The regenerative braking system converts the kinetic energy of the vehicle 1A

into electrical energy, 1A

(c) Since the car maintains a constant speed, its KE remains unchanged.

Work done against the braking system

= loss in GPE = 1800 × 9.81 × 15 1M

= 264 900 J

Energy stored = 264 900 × 32%

= 84.8 kJ 1A

(d) The refuelling time of a hybrid vehicle is much shorter. 1A

It has a longer range. 1A

(Or other reasonable answers)

tb-E303-21.question:
In countries with long periods of cold weather like Britain, solar control window films can be employed to reduce heat transfer from the interior to the exterior of the building.

(a) Give an advantage of solar control window films over tinted glasses. (1 mark)

(b) Should the films be installed on windows that receive more sunlight or less sunlight? Explain briefly. (2 marks)

(c) The installation of double-glazed windows is more important in Britain than in Hong Kong. Why? (2 marks)
tb-E303-21.answer:
(a) Solar control window films allow more visible light to enter the building. 1A

(b) The film should be installed on windows that receive less sunlight. 1A

This allows more sunlight to enter the building and makes the building warmer. 1A

(c) Double-glazed windows reduce heat transfer by conduction. 1A

In Britain, heat loss by conduction through windows is more significant. 1A

tb-E303-23.question:
According to the regulations in Hong Kong, the OTTV for a building envelope should not exceed 21 W m–2.

(a) What is the meaning of the OTTV of a building envelope? (1 mark)

(b) Figure l shows the design of a cylindrical building. The height of the building is 63 m. The walls and the roof are made of concrete. The windows are distributed as shown. The U-value of the concrete part is 4.1 W m–2 K–1. The rate of heat transfer per unit area through the windows is 140 W m–2.

(i) Does the OTTV of this building comply with the regulations in Hong Kong? Show your calculation. Take the equivalent temperature difference to be 6 K. (4 marks)

(ii) Suggest two methods to lower the OTTV of the building. (2 marks)
tb-E303-23.answer:
(a) OTTV is the average rate of heat gain per unit area into a building through the building envelope by both conduction and radiation. 1A

(b) (i) Rate of heat transfer through concrete part

= UA (TH − TC) 1M

= (4.1)(2π × 20 ×632+ π × 202)(6)

= 1.283 × 105 W

≈ 1.28 × 105 W

Rate of heat transfer through windows

= 140 × (2π × 20 ×632)

= 5.542 × 105 W

≈ 5.54 × 105 W

OTTV of the building

= (QCt + QSt) ÷ AT 1M

= 1.283 × 105 + 5.542 × 1052π × 20 × 63 + π × 202

= 74.4 W m−2 (> 21 W m−2) 1A

Therefore, the OTTV of this building does not comply with the regulations in Hong Kong. 1A

(ii) Use light-coloured paint for outer surfaces. 1A

Use double-glazed windows 1A

(Or other reasonable answers)

tb-E303-24.question:
A bedroom in a flat has only one wall facing outside. The wall has two windows (Fig m). The area of the wall (excluding the windows) is 10 m2 and the total area of the windows is 6 m2. An air conditioner is turned on and the room temperature is maintained at 25 °C. The temperature of the outside surface of the wall is 33 °C. The U-value of the wall is 1.2 W m–2 K–1. The rate of heat transfer per unit area through the windows is 157 W m−2. The rate of heat generated by indoor equipment is 500 W.

(a) Estimate the total rate of heat exchange between the inside and outside of the bedroom. Assume the heat transfer through the other walls, the ceiling and the floor is negligible. (4 marks)

(b) Estimate the cooling capacity of the air conditioner. (2 marks)

(c) Suggest three methods to reduce the energy consumption of the air conditioner. (3 marks)
tb-E303-24.answer:
(a) Rate of heat transfer through wall

= UA (TH − TC) 1M

= 1.2 × 10 (33 − 25)

= 96 W 1M

Rate of heat transfer through windows

= 157 × 6

= 942 W 1M

Total rate of heat exchange

= 96 + 942

= 1038 = 1040 W 1A

(b) Cooling capacity

= 1038 + 500 1M

= 1538 = 1540 W 1A

(c) Install solar control window films to the windows. 1A

Install a layer of mineral wool to the wall. 1A

Turn off the equipment that is not in used. 1A

(Or other reasonable answers)

tb-E303-26.question:
Figure o shows a Korean BBQ restaurant. The door and the windows are made of the same kind of glass and their total area is 60 m2. The temperature of the exterior surface of the building envelope is 32 °C. An air conditioner is turned on so that the interior of the restaurant is maintained at 25 °C.

(a) The walls and the roof are 20 cm thick and they have the same U-value of 1.2 W m–2 K–1. The heat transfer per unit area through the windows and the door is 100 W m–2. Estimate the total rate of heat transfer through the building envelope. (3 marks)

(b) There are 10 electric grills in the restaurant. Each grill releases heat inside the restaurant at a rate of 800 W. Assume there is no other heat source in the restaurant.

(i) How is the OTTV of the building affected by the grills? (1 mark)

(ii) If all the grills are turned on, estimate the cooling capacity of the air conditioner. (2 marks)
tb-E303-26.answer:
(a) Rate of heat transfer through walls and roof

= UA (TH − TC) 1M

= 1.2 × (20 × 10 + 20 × 3 × 2 + 3 × 10 × 2 − 60) × (32 − 25)

= 2688 W

Total rate of heat transfer

= 2688 + 100 × 60

= 8690 W 1A

(b) (i) The OTTV is not affected by the grills. 1A

(ii) Cooling capacity

= 8690 + 800 × 10 1M

= 16 700 W 1A
